pr_body:
fixes #18112

It's the same behaviour as if you create a branch: empty commit list but the head commit is the last commit.

I'm not sure about the compare url. With `git.EmptySHA` you will see a 404 page. GitHub displays a "There isn’t anything to compare" page in this case.

issue_context.title: Tag push creates webhook with empty `commits` and `head_commit`
issue_context.body:
### Gitea Version

1.15.8

### Git Version

2.33.1

### Operating System

Windows Server 2016

### How are you running Gitea?

based on gitea-1.15.8-windows-4.0-amd64.exe as Windows Service

### Database

SQLite

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

Yes

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Description

Creating a new tag for a gitea repo creates a webhook with empty `commits` and `head_commit`. See example from gitea demo site:
```
{
  "ref": "refs/tags/v1.1.1",
  "before": "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  "after": "3f150d39b92dd50cdd0248f5edea5767c2172584",
  "compare_url": "https://try.gitea.io/",
  "commits": [],
  "head_commit": null,
  "repository": {
  ...
```

I have an on-prem gitea instance connected with on-prem AppVeyor server. AppVeyor can't create new builds if  `commits` and `head_commit` are empty, see also open issue on AppVeyor: appveyor/ci#3765

### Screenshots

_No response_
comments: Just tested newest Gitea main build (1.16.0+dev-785-g496acbe9e) and AppVeyor is still not triggering a new build for a new tag. AppVeyor seems to expect both `commits` and `head_commit` to be defined.

@KN4CK3R AppVeyor Server was updated with version 7.0.3134 to support `head_commit` in the webhook payload. With that change AppVeyor Server is creating a build for a Gitea tag webhook again. See also appveyor/ci#3765.
Thanks for fixing the Gitea part!

review_comments:
It's surprising that `NewPushCommits` only creates an empty struct ....

And the code below duplicates. Could we introduce some more meaningful functions?

ps: I can accept that what the code does, if there is a chance, maybe we can clarify the code.
How would you deduplicate it? There may be a method which sets the head commit in the "constructor" but the compare url needs too many parameters. Feel free to change it.

How about:

```
func NewPushCommitsForNotification(commit) {
	commits := repository.NewPushCommits()
	commits.HeadCommit = repository.CommitToPushCommit(commit)
	commits.CompareURL = rel.Repo.ComposeCompareURL(git.EmptySHA, commit.ID.String())
	return commits
}
```
But that name would be wrong for the "deleted ref" notification or `push.go@200`.
